notes: EXCLUDED: study_type = experimental_evolution. The 49 ENA samples classified as Klebsiella are Raoultella sp.1 and sp.2 isolates (Raoultella is a genus formerly nested within Klebsiella and still classified there by some ENA taxonomic assignments), comprising both ancestral clones and evolved populations after 5 months of deliberate experimental evolution in dialysis-bag laboratory microcosms. Focal strains were originally isolated from water-filled tree holes in south England (August 2013–April 2014) and then deliberately evolved under pH 5.5 selective pressure while interacting chemically with complex background communities. No AMR selection criterion was used; all isolates are environmental with no human hosts, so amr_study, amr_target, amr_method, and cohort_age are not applicable. EBI title cites 69 Raoultella isolates versus 49 in ENA and 47 stated in the paper — minor metadata discrepancy, likely reflecting removal of some samples or counting convention differences; no evidence of a multi-accession split or umbrella accession issue.

study_type.evidence_quote: Rather than regularly transferring a small proportion of the population to fresh media, in the style of classical experimental evolution, we replaced only 10% of the medium once per week to mimic natural conditions. We created a living archive of frozen samples collected from the dialysis bags over the 5 months. By comparing the growth, metabolic phenotype (i.e. degradation of labile vs. recalcitrant carbon sources) and the genotype of the evolved population to those of the ancestral strains, we assessed both the tempo and mode of evolution of focal strains.

Per-accession breakdown is not given; the number attributable to PRJEB42370 cannot be determined (Scenario C: umbrella/shared accession). Coverage is far below 75%.

notes: PRJEB42370 is one of six ENA accessions (PRJEB59013, PRJEB43549, PRJEB50554, PRJEB42370, PRJEB43550, PRJEB60429) deposited from a single longitudinal German hospital study of VIM-CPE (2018–2021). Sizing sanity check: the paper describes 12 Klebsiella isolates in total across all 6 accessions, yet PRJEB42370 alone holds 34 Klebsiella by ENA count — Scenario C (umbrella/shared accession; ENA count far exceeds paper count). Paper coverage of this accession's Klebsiella records is far below 75%; all study-level attributes are therefore graded 'partial'. The EBI title '2019: routine sample from the IIMK' anchors the collection year to 2019 for this accession. The EBI description ('detect multi-resistant microorganism and control the spread') together with the paper's CPE-selective inclusion criteria (patients positive for VIM-CPE by carbapenemase PCR) support amr_study = amr and amr_method = pcr_gene_presence. The paper's patients are all adults (mean age 73, range 27–80), supporting cohort_age = adult, but only as partial given coverage. Isolation source is mixed (clinical diagnostic specimens plus rectal screening swabs) with no single dominant source determinable for the accession as a whole; proposed_value set to null.
